stem:
Farhan looks at the diagram. Straight line $AOB$ meets at $O$, and ray $OP$ cuts the straight angle into adjacent angles $\angle AOP$ and $\angle POB$. The marked angle $\angle POB$ is $65^{\circ}$.

Which claim correctly finds $\angle AOP$?

options.text: Call the answer the ray $OP$, and stop.
Finding $\angle AOP$ is what creates the straight line $AOB$.
$\angle AOP=180^{\circ}-65^{\circ}=115^{\circ}$, because adjacent angles on a straight line make $180^{\circ}$.
$\angle AOP=65^{\circ}$, matching the largest printed degree mark in the diagram.

teacher.key_rationale: Adjacent angles on a straight line sum to 180°, so ∠AOP=180−65=115. Naming the ray, reversing cause, or copying the printed 65 miss that whole-angle split.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangles as straight line AOB with ray OP and marked adjacent angle 65°.
